projects.rationale: Pohang Phase I began in April 1970 as a long, externally financed integrated steel project. The extra industrial level extends its production base and makes the credit exposure concrete.
A reinforced grid is a paid enabling investment for concentrated industrial demand; the treasury bears its setup cost.
A paid dispatchable plant supports Yeongnam industry; the existing energy programme carries its financing exposure and does not grant free fuel or raw resources.
A paid production line in Yeongnam gives electronics exports a tangible manufacturing base while the existing education cost and export concentration remain.
The freight programme now links central and southwestern provinces as well as Seoul and Yeongnam; its upfront public cost and interest exposure are retained.
Performance-reviewed Saemaul grants fund one shared agricultural facility in the southwest; output is tied to local project selection and state oversight.
The urban welfare route pairs service coverage with a Seoul metropolitan service facility and recurring fiscal obligations.
The rural insurance route pairs farm-community coverage with an agricultural service base, at a public setup and recurring social cost.
Directed conglomerate credit builds concentrated heavy-industry capacity; its greater interest exposure and bureaucracy represent public guarantees and concentrated access.
Competitive credit builds provincial banking and procurement capacity instead of another Yeongnam production line, while accepting slower scale and administration costs.
The conservative parliamentary settlement funds a regional access link alongside its existing Honam industrial project.
The social-democratic provincial programme adds a shared farm service base alongside the Honam industrial investment, with welfare funding obligations preserved.
The small-enterprise option places new supplier capacity in Chungcheong and cuts financing exposure, trading conglomerate scale for a broader regional base.
The large-industry option adds concentrated Yeongnam capacity and output, with larger credit and political-concentration costs than the small-firm route.
The revolutionary reconstruction programme funds access infrastructure alongside its existing Chungcheong industry, while retaining its planned-economy and trade costs.
Air-cover procurement reduces the cost of the installed MD fighter family and grants one bounded aircraft research use; readiness and alliance dependence remain policy costs.
The escort doctrine receives a narrow frigate procurement discount and one naval research use; it does not grant hulls or free shipyards.
The mobile force option receives one limited armored-vehicle research use and a narrow medium-chassis cost reduction, offset by its existing fuel, equipment, and upkeep exposure.
Counterbattery investment receives a finite artillery research use and a modest artillery-equipment cost reduction, while retaining the training and support burden.
The petrochemical leg funds a refinery in Yeongnam to connect chemical industrialisation with power and steel demand. It is paid construction, not a free resource or uranium grant.
A paid Chungcheong production line anchors the machine-tool and component programme outside the main export core; credit and skill shortages remain binding trade-offs.

entries.rationale: A limited planning office improves productive capacity while adding a modest administrative burden.
Heavy industry creates a durable output gain, paid for through greater credit exposure.
Export electronics reward production learning and output, while technical education costs and reliance on imported methods remain.
Domestic electronics capability improves learning and production efficiency but needs continued technical instruction.
Light export diversification raises civilian production and reduces reliance on subsidized capital, with less strategic output than the heavy-industry route.
The integrated steel project raises national industrial capacity but concentrates public credit in a long construction cycle.
Provincial export capacity improves industrial output while requiring more regional administration.
Transport links accelerate later construction and output, with borrowing costs for the network.
Engineering capacity improves technical adaptation and reduces training costs, while limiting reliance on external advisers.
Applied colleges increase research capacity and lower skill-training costs, requiring sustained public administration.
Factory-linked laboratories raise industrial learning and efficiency, with continuing technical education costs.
Trade training raises factory productivity and reduces the labour needed per building, financed through lower-cost practical instruction.
Village works improve agricultural productivity and local confidence, but the campaign expands state administration.
Cooperative purchasing and extension services improve rural yields and reduce household support costs, with a larger administrative footprint.
Measured grants reward productive local projects and improve state capacity, while increasing reporting and allocation costs.
Public village accounts improve trust and agricultural coordination while reducing waste in the programme.
Large export firms can mobilize capital and scale quickly, at the cost of concentrated bargaining power and heavier oversight.
Performance-based credit lowers financing friction and rewards productive firms, while limiting discretionary patronage.
Export targets raise industrial sales and trade access, redirecting some production away from domestic consumption.
Supplier guarantees widen domestic industrial capacity, with contingent credit exposure for the treasury.
Supplier engineering raises productivity and expands the industrial base while smaller firms depend on credit guarantees.
Shared quality standards improve factory efficiency and reduce building labour requirements, supported by inspection staff.
A stronger planning board coordinates investment and technical forecasts, funded by a larger civil service.
Rural and urban investment narrows regional gaps, trading a smaller peak in export concentration for broader stability.
Competitive procurement lowers project costs and patronage, while due process slows decisions and requires audit staff.
Contributory pensions strengthen household security, with payroll and public-finance costs.
Transparent tax administration improves compliance and trust but reduces short-term executive discretion.
Civilian oversight strengthens constitutional authority while requiring the armed forces to adjust to new command relations.
Disclosure improves financial confidence and public accountability, with added regulatory work.
Broad social protection reduces household insecurity but raises recurring fiscal commitments.
Means-tested support protects the most exposed households at lower direct cost, requiring more administrative screening.
Negotiated labour relations reduce disruption and improve output, sharing some policy authority with organised workers.
Workplace councils raise cooperation and productivity while creating a formal dispute-resolution burden.
Market discipline improves credit allocation and business output but exposes protected sectors to adjustment.
Institutional continuity steadies the governing coalition while slowing contested academic reform.
A negotiated security settlement keeps command institutions functional while constraining presidential control.
Universal coverage improves household security with higher health-finance commitments.
Contributions broaden coverage more gradually, adding payroll administration while limiting general-revenue exposure.
Public development credit supports productive investment and lowers financing costs, with a larger oversight obligation.
Cooperative ownership broadens industrial participation at the cost of some centralized direction.
Rationalization improves capacity and plant efficiency while refinancing redundant investment.
Professional staff training improves cohesion and recovery while placing military expertise inside more formal institutions.
Removing political appointments strengthens civilian legitimacy but disrupts command and requires a funded transition.
Civilian defence administration improves accountability and political control, with added staffing and coordination costs.
A larger reserve pool expands mobilization at the expense of training time and equipment expenditure.
A smaller professional core raises readiness and recovery with higher personnel costs.
Crew proficiency improves mission effectiveness but requires more aircraft upkeep and trained personnel.
Escort doctrine improves fleet coordination at a higher supply and equipment cost.
Improved fire control raises artillery effectiveness while consuming more ammunition and supply.
Joint air command improves sortie coordination while requiring more equipment and staff.
Joint staff procedures improve army organization and grant one limited land-doctrine study reduction, with a larger staff burden.
Domestic defence production builds arms capacity and factory output while retaining a bounded public-credit burden.
Changwon expands Korean arms production with licensed small-arms and artillery cost reductions, one finite research use in each supported family, and a modest financing burden.
Judicial safeguards improve legitimacy while narrowing the security service’s freedom to collect intelligence.
Protected records strengthen institutional security and public confidence, requiring permanent custodial staff.
Coalition brokerage improves legislative throughput at the cost of cabinet compromise and additional coordination.
An independent party earns broader acceptance and industrial investment while giving up some executive leverage.
Regional credit improves farm productivity and lowers financing friction, with more local supervision required.
Small firms receive market access and technical finance, with slower capacity growth than the large-industry programme.
Large projects raise capacity and output quickly, while increasing public-credit concentration.
Supplier networks connect smaller firms to industrial contracts and require stronger procurement oversight.
Export compromise increases industrial sales and trade access, redirecting some output away from domestic consumption.
Production cadres direct resources into state industry, gaining capacity at the cost of financing risk and labour conflict.
Worker elections improve cooperation and output while distributing political authority through workplace institutions.
Joint planning coordinates industrial and agricultural production, while closer political alignment narrows external options.
A negotiated settlement strengthens internal stability and industrial continuity, requiring new administrative institutions.
A disciplined vanguard mobilizes political authority and security capacity but narrows social acceptance.
Pluralist socialist institutions broaden consent and protect policy autonomy while sharing executive power.

domestic_cost_scale.scope: Convert positive national focus effects.cost amounts to GDP shares. Foreign agreement terms and recipient charges remain in the bilateral contract records and are unchanged.
domestic_cost_scale.reason: The 1970 Korean GDP baseline is about 9.085 billion. Legacy flat national focus prices of one to six billion represented an excessive share of the real starting economy.
